reviewed.name: Petz Shared Core
reviewed.finding: packages/petz-bridge/src/mascot-bridge.ts loads persistence by breedId, does not restore the loaded object, and destroy() saves full engine serialization under generated pet.id keys. The inspected bridge therefore cannot prove restart restore and has a load/save identity mismatch in addition to the explicit restore TODO.
reviewed.action: Opened GameSync-Next issue #9 with a preservation-first repair contract: explicit stable persistence identity, non-destructive single-pet restore, multi-pet/same-breed coverage, corrupt-save fallback, host build/typecheck, and real restart proof.
reviewed.acceptance: A saved pet restores exact Petz-owned state after restart; two same-breed pets persist independently; restoring one pet never clears another; affected hosts load the changed build and pass restart/runtime verification.

reviewed.name: RuneLite QA Cockpit
reviewed.finding: Current RuneLite Plugin Hub guidance still recommends Java 11, commit-pinned hub manifests, latest.release, and dependency verification. Current jqwik upstream is now in pure maintenance mode and version 1.10 adds an Anti-AI Usage Clause, making it a weaker fit for an agent-driven QA cockpit. JQF remains active through July 2026, supports JUnit 5 fuzz tests, and provides coverage-guided semantic fuzzing via Zest.
reviewed.proposal: After the canonical QA Cockpit source is recovered and its existing tests are green, evaluate JQF as an isolated generated-content QA lane for route/step/content invariants rather than adding a stale or agent-hostile property-testing dependency blindly.
reviewed.acceptance: The recovered plugin remains Plugin-Hub compatible; bounded normal tests replay saved fuzz regressions; fuzzing finds malformed/orphan/identity failures without changing shipping content or runtime behavior.

projectConstellationResearch.problem: PRJ-002 demonstrates that a detailed project wiki can remain internally coherent yet lag stronger project-owned evidence by several verified generations.
projectConstellationResearch.proposal: Add a read-only freshness auditor that compares each project catalog/wiki latest-verified claim against newer project-owned checkpoints, repository heads/releases, research cursor evidence, and Drive artifacts. It should surface stale-latest claims, evidence date/hash, stronger candidate authority, and the exact reconciliation action without mutating project content.
projectConstellationResearch.acceptance: Detects the V24-vs-V33 PRJ-002 drift; never promotes by timestamp alone; user edits remain authoritative; exactly 63 projects remain; no presentation artifact is rewritten merely because a warning exists.
